newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds close stronger but underperform U.S.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds close stronger but underperform U.S.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger on Thursday, rebounding from early losses caused by foreign selling, on strength in U.S. fixed income markets following positive economic data there, analysts said.

"We got our strength from the U.S. Treasuries," said Cameron Laird, vice president of bond investments with Zurich Canada Investment Management Ltd. "As the Treasury market rallied that did pull us up."
Canada's 30-year bond rose C$0.50 to C$108.25 to yield 7.290 percent. The U.S. 30-year bond rose 1- 4/32 to yield 6.75 percent.
The spread between the bonds widened to 54 basis points from 49 basis points at the close of trading on Wednesday.

Canadian bonds had opened weaker in the wake of overnight selling and sharply underperformed U.S. Treasuries at the beginning of the session. However, strength in U.S. bonds following this morning's tame U.S. producer price index report pulled Canada into positive territory near the time that markets in Europe were closing.
"It seemed to indicate us that there was selling pressure coming from offshore," said Joe Lee, a bond portfolio manager with Laketon Investment Management.

All eyes are now on U.S. and Canadian December employment data, which is being released tomorrow morning, analysts said. In the past the reports, seen as a key indicators of the economy's strength, have prompted sharp movements in bond prices.

In other economic news, a report today showed Canadian housing starts fell by a lower-than-expected 1.1 percent in December. A second report showed Canada's help wanted index rose by a higher-than-expected 3.0 percent in November.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 rose C$0.33 to C$102.33 to yield 6.673 percent.
The U.S. 10-year bond rose 21/32 to yield 6.50 percent. The spread between the benchmark bonds widened to 17 basis points from 14 basis points at the close of trading on Wednesday.
The three-month cash bill traded with a yield of 2.86 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.12 percent.
